title: Candy pop — settle the identity system
question: Candy pop is picked. The one open conflict: neon blocks and brand cubes compete for the same glance. Four resolutions, each with a single governing rule — pick the rule you want the rail to obey.

options.label: Candy · Brand blocks
options.lineage: channel-branded tiles — the app's own colour IS the tile
options.thesis: One system: the app's brand paints the block; cubes are gone; a plain letter rides the block corner.
options.viewport: Black page, white clock, cyan P100; blocks painted in real brand colours (YouTube red, Netflix red, Prime blue, Crunchyroll orange, Spotify green, Plex amber); big initial letters replace cubes; white outline marks selection.
options.risk: YouTube and Netflix are both red — the name and number must carry the difference.

options.label: Candy · Brand duotone
options.lineage: duotone branding systems — one hue, two intensities
options.thesis: One system at two depths: the block is the brand hue darkened, the cube the same hue saturated — depth, not competition.
options.viewport: Black page; each block muted-deep in its own brand hue (dark red for YouTube, wine for Netflix, deep blue Prime...), the cube above it blazing the same hue at full brand saturation; white names; selection outline white.
options.risk: Muted hues can look muddy side by side if the darkening isn't consistent across all six.

options.label: Candy · Quiet rail
options.lineage: instrument rails — the rail is chrome, the lamps carry colour
options.thesis: Strict job split: blocks near-black, ONLY cubes carry brand colour; the launcher's own neon lives solely in chrome (cues, clock accents, selection).
options.viewport: Black page; six near-black blocks with white brand cubes and names; the candy pigment appears only as cyan P100, amber P110 cue, white selection outline and green LIVE dot.
options.risk: Quietest of the four — loses the candy exuberance the pick was chosen for.

options.label: Candy · Channel index
options.lineage: broadcast channel line-ups — the station paints its own numbers, brands irrelevant
options.thesis: Brands excluded: colour belongs to the PAGE NUMBER, fixed forever (101 red, 102 violet, 103 cyan...) — apps are channels on your home's line-up.
options.viewport: Black page; block colour determined by page number alone, whatever app sits there; neutral white cube with black letter; muscle memory: red is always 101, violet always 102.
options.risk: Zero brand signal — recognisable only to you; a re-pin changes which app wears which colour.
